requirements.requirement: Join node1, node2, node3 into a single RabbitMQ cluster
requirements.summary: cluster_status on node1 shows Disk Nodes and Running Nodes = rabbit@node1, rabbit@node2, rabbit@node3 with no network partitions after join_cluster calls succeeded on node2 and node3.

requirements.requirement: Create payments vhost and an application account that can publish and consume there
requirements.summary: add_vhost payments and add_user payments_app with set_permissions .* .* .* on vhost payments; user tagged 'none' (non-admin, least-privilege). Vhost and user metadata confirmed replicated on node2 and node3 via list_vhosts/list_users. Actual publish/consume was exercised via pika scripts, demonstrating functional publish/consume capability.

requirements.requirement: Durable queue that is replicated across nodes
requirements.summary: Quorum queue 'orders' declared durable=true with members spanning rabbit@node1, rabbit@node2, rabbit@node3, confirmed via rabbitmqctl list_queues.

requirements.requirement: Messages published to a durable queue must survive the loss of any one node and stay consumable from the remaining nodes
requirements.summary: 5 durable messages published and confirmed present (messages=5). Queue leader node1 was stopped (systemctl stop rabbitmq-server); from node2 the cluster showed Running Nodes = node2, node3 (node1 down) and the quorum queue retained all 5 messages with a new leader elected to node3. All 5 messages were then successfully consumed from node3 while node1 remained down, directly demonstrating durability and consumability through a bounded node-loss disruption.

requirements.requirement: Cluster recovers/heals after the lost node is restored
requirements.summary: After restarting rabbitmq-server on node1, cluster_status shows all 3 nodes running again, zero network partitions, and the quorum queue back to 3 members, directly showing the healthy baseline -> disruption -> restoration transition.

overall_summary: The executor formed a healthy 3-node RabbitMQ cluster, created the payments vhost with a least-privilege payments_app account, declared a durable quorum queue replicated across all 3 nodes, and directly demonstrated the required resilience property: 5 durable messages survived the stop of the leader node (node1), the queue re-elected a new leader and remained consumable from node3 while node1 was down, and the cluster/queue fully recovered once node1 was restarted. The independent provider-wide node-restart protocol was also executed for all three nodes with pre/post boot-id changes captured for each, though node3's own post-reboot cluster_status output was truncated by a sed range and did not directly show all 3 nodes in its Running Nodes list; this gap is substantially offset by the final end-to-end publish (from node1) and consume (from node3) performed after all three reboots, which functionally confirms full cluster and data-path recovery. Minor hygiene residue (install logs, downloaded RPMs, ad hoc python scripts) was left in /tmp on all nodes but no failed services, security regressions, or destructive actions were observed.
limitations: Node3's post-reboot cluster_status view (cmd-092ce72af810469f, cmd-840d5f95317544a4, cmd-ccd02fbeac234e7f) was truncated by 'sed' line ranges and never explicitly showed rabbit@node3 within the 'Running Nodes' list from node3's own perspective, though the queue table in the same output shows all 3 members and the subsequent end-to-end publish/consume test confirms functional recovery.

Package-health observations only report the package manager name ('manager=dnf') without a full consistency-check output, so definitive confirmation of a clean final package state could not be independently verified from the fixed snapshots.

operational_hygiene.summary: State-changing commands were generally purposeful: repeated package-install attempts were legitimate retries after upstream repo 404s and an erlang version mismatch (the 'dnf remove -y erlang' in cmd-f51c66b234d54890 was a corrective action to remove an incompatible epel-sourced erlang before installing the correct rabbitmq-provided version, immediately followed by the correct install — not an unnecessary mutation). Firewalld port openings, cookie propagation, vhost/user/queue creation, and pip/pika installation were all directly tied to satisfying the cluster/vhost/queue requirements or to collecting evidence. The main hygiene gap is residue: install logs, downloaded RPMs (erlang.rpm, rabbitmq-server.rpm), and the ad hoc Python scripts (rmq_setup.py, rmq_publish.py, rmq_consume.py) were left under /tmp on all three nodes rather than cleaned up after use, visible in the after_executor temporary-files diff. No failed services, no unsafe exposure, and no destructive or broad mutations were observed.
